fieldValues.title: How a remedy differs by domain and persona
fieldValues.thinking_reached: A problem can occur in several domains and be held by many personas (decision 708c9373, proposed). A remedy, however, may be different in different domains for different people. Today a remedy only answers a problem; nothing records which domain or persona it is for.
fieldValues.tensions: Meaning that must stay stable belongs in relations, not container membership (two-domain plan, what we learned); the owner also suggested building these maps with containers. Cloning a problem per domain keeps remedies simple but splits one claim into drifting copies.
fieldValues.unresolved_questions: 1. Does a remedy name who it is for, e.g. a relation remedy for persona-in-domain? 2. Or does a domain container place its remedies in its outline, under the problems they answer? 3. Or is a problem cloned per domain when its remedies diverge? 4. Must an epic then serve one domain, or may it implement remedies from several?
fieldValues.blocking: Nothing yet: today's remedies each sit in one domain. It blocks once a remedy is suggested for a problem held in two domains.
fieldValues.next_action: Recommendation for the owner's next session: option 1 (a relation from remedy to the persona-in-domain it serves), because it states meaning as a relation and needs no clones; the domain container may show it as arrangement. Needs one method package relation type.
